author: Fairly shy
text_post: However, that will only work if there are other words that can be used, that cover the full range of meanings of the excluded word. Unless that is true, the rationalist position is to simple avoid certain subjects! An obvious example is the word 'consciousness'. For many years psychology avoided the word by talking about behaviourism. However, it seems generally accepted that that strategy failed - it boxed psychology in far too much. One of the puzzles about consciousness, is how a piece of physical matter can actually have experiences (as opposed to merely absorbing data). You can eliminate that problem by banning the word 'consciousness', but clearly by doing so, you exclude subjects that are obviously worth discussing - how exactly would you produce a machine/computer that would feel happy/sad/pain/pleasure? FS

author: MathAutist
text_post: The point of the rationalist taboo is to enable discussions without getting bogged down in arguing about the meanings of certain words, not to shut down discussions.

author: Fairly shy
text_post: I am sure that is what is intended, but I have seen so many people try to squash discussions about consciousness by asking for a precise definition of consciousness (which is rather like making the word taboo, by replacing it by some, inevitably inadequate, definition). Now if we were talking about Gibb's free energy, or something, a precise definition would be really useful, but it doesn't really help with some concepts. This is because some concepts don't really fit within the standard materialist framework, so if you demand a materialist definition, you instantly distort it. I think it is probably the case that consciousness can't be explained materialistically - the world would make a lot more sense if consciousness didn't exist (forgetting for the moment that we would not be around to observe it!). The 'rational' crowd go through hoops to explain consciousness away - some of them tell you free will doesn't exist, some would like to tell you that a thermostat is 'conscious' to the extent that it 'decides' to turn the heat on and off when it is needed, etc. To me, that is just BS! However, I am one of those fruitcakes that believes some paranormal phenomena are real! FS
